title: Coastal homeowners and offshore wind power: voting, behavior change, and compensation
Private versus public flood insurance: differences in premiums and uptake in two coastal housing markets using survey data
abstract: Using a natural experiment created by the 1982 Coastal Barrier Resources Act (CBRA), we measure the extent to which insurance premiums vary between private and publicly backed flood insurance policies. The CBRA resulted in homeowners living in neighboring housing markets in which some have access to the federally backed National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and others do not. Flood risks and other features of the neighborhoods are otherwise indistinguishable. Those without access to publicly backed insurance must purchase private insurance if they desire coverage. We compare insurance premiums and uptake in the two markets and find that premiums for private coverage are significantly higher than public rates (after controlling for other factors in a reduced-form regression), implying a subsidy by NFIP. We also find a much lower uptake of insurance in the areas without federally backed insurance. Our results are based on a mail survey of residents in two US coastal communities with a 50% response rate: North Bethany Beach, Delaware, and North Topsail Beach, North Carolina. We also present results related to perceptions of flood hazards, of being under- or overinsured, and measures taken to mitigate flood damage.
abstract_zh: 利用1982年《沿海屏障资源法》（CBRA）所创造的自然实验，我们衡量了私人与公共支持的洪水保险保费之间的差异程度。该法案使相邻住房市场中的居民处境不同：一些人可以获得联邦支持的国家洪水保险计划（NFIP）的保障，另一些人则不能。这些社区的洪水风险及其他特征在其他方面并无差异。无法获得公共支持保险的人若想投保，必须购买私人保险。我们比较了两个市场中的保费和投保率，发现私人保险的保费显著高于公共费率（在回归分析中控制其他因素后），这意味着NFIP存在补贴。我们还发现，在没有联邦支持保险的地区，投保率低得多。我们的结果基于对美国两个沿海社区居民的邮寄调查，回复率为50%，这两个社区分别是特拉华州的北贝瑟海滩和北卡罗来纳州的北托普赛尔海滩。我们还呈现了与洪水风险认知、对投保不足或过度投保的感知，以及为减轻洪水损失而采取的措施相关的结果。
